messages:
kevin: Heads-up — short spike of NVIDIA Xid 13 and 31 in us-east1 on the A10 pool around 18:00 UTC. Opening thread to gather signals.

maria: Thanks. Which hosts and how many GPUs impacted? Any obvious model/workload pattern?

kevin: ~8 GPUs across three hosts (g4-us-east1-12, -20, -21). Mostly Xid 13, a few Xid 31. Timeline ~18:00–18:07 UTC. Workloads: mixed long decode (beam/greedy loops seq=1024) + a batched eval job.

infra-bot: Alert: GPU_ERROR_COUNT increased on pool=g4-us-east1, hosts=[g4-us-east1-12,g4-us-east1-20,g4-us-east1-21]

jordan: Can someone paste nvidia-smi -q + dmesg snippets and driver/kernel versions?

kevin: paste logs:

```
# nvidia-smi -q --gpu=0
Product Name : NVIDIA A10
Driver Version: 535.86
Attached GPUs : 1

GPU 00000000:3B:00.0
    Xid Error: 13 (MCE): CEC error during channel parity
```

and dmesg excerpt:

```
[Sun Mar 24 18:00:02] NVRM: Xid (13): 79fd0000 00000000 00000000 00000000
[Sun Mar 24 18:00:05] NVRM: Xid (31): 00000000 00000000 00000000
```

maria: Xid 13/31 cluster-level pattern could be ECC flaps or a driver/kernel scheduling issue hitting microcode paths. These hosts are on 535.86 — we've seen 535.x oddities on A10 before.

sre-oncall: Quick triage I ran:
- cordoned g4-us-east1-12 and migrated pods
- repro with synthetic long-attn decode: saw 1 Xid13 after ~800k tokens on spare node

devops: Are these using int8 kernels or fused flash-attn decode? Kernel codepath matters for repro.

jordan: Job metadata shows eval job used tensor-quant int8 + flash-attention fused kernels (runtime: batch=16, seq=1024, kv-cache on). Xids align with high decode throughput.

kevin: kernel log snippet:

```
[18:01:12] gpu:0 compute: invalid read in cuLaunchKernel at warp 12
[18:01:12] gpu:0 Xid(13) -> MIGRATION
```

maria: Ops checklist:
1) collect full dmesg + gpu logs for hosts (kevin: uploaded?)
2) check ECC counters (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory_errors.corrected) — look low but rising on host-20
3) repro on spare with same driver and try disabling fused-kernel path

kevin: uploaded logs to /mnt/ops/xid-us-east1/1843210001.tar.gz. ECC counters:

```
host-12: corrected=4, uncorrected=0
host-20: corrected=28, uncorrected=0
host-21: corrected=5, uncorrected=1
```

sre-oncall: host-21 has uncorrected=1. Marking that GPU as flaky — plan drain + RMA. host-20 corrected count suggests memory noise; run memtest and firmware checks.

devops: Proposed remediation:
- Drain host-21 immediately (cordon + migrate), open RMA ticket for that GPU index
- Move host-20 to maintenance, run extended cuda-memtest and firmware update if failures
- Roll forward driver to 535.102 on a canary node and run synthetic repro

maria: Correlation note: most Xid events co-occur with beam_size >=4 and seq >=512 under int8 + fused kernels. Could be a race in fused decoder + kv-cache. Recommend temporary workload mitigation: cap beam_size or disable fused kernels for long-decode eval jobs.

kevin: I'll push a scheduler override to set fused_kernels=false and beam_max=4 for job_tag=eval-long-decode.

jordan: Checked networking: no packet drops, PCIe errors look clean — not a fabric blip.

infra-bot: Deploy change applied: runtime override for job_tag=eval-long-decode -> fused_kernels=false, beam_max=4

sre-oncall: host-21 GPU queued for replacement, host-20 memtest running. Post-change: no new Xid events in canary pool for ~8h. Looks promising.

devops: Filing follow-up telemetry work: capture kernel symbol / exact cuLaunchKernel names and runtime flags per job to correlate Xid codes to kernel names. Filing IT-2145.

kevin: TL;DR: short spike of Xid13/31 tied to decode-heavy int8 fused-kernel workloads on A10s. Actions: drained/replaced flaky GPU, maintenance + memtest for noisy node, temporary runtime mitigations, follow-up telemetry ticket.

maria: I'll draft a short postmortem to postmortems/ with repro steps and kernel snippets.

kevin: tagging @sre-oncall @devops for visibility :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Closing triage thread — reopen if events recur.
summary: A short-lived cluster spike of NVIDIA Xid 13/31 on A10s in us-east1 during decode-heavy int8 workloads. Root cause suspected: interaction between fused decoder kernels + kv-cache under high throughput and possible intermittent memory noise. Remedies: drain/replace flaky GPU, maintenance + memtest, temporary runtime flag overrides (disable fused kernels, cap beam), driver canary, and follow-up telemetry ticket.
